page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core and memory performance alongside weaker single-core capabilities. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 8268.09 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 6983.38, both falling into the average tier. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 389.93 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 37.84 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is limited, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1150.0 and a weak Redis SET throughput of 6.84 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r6.2xlarge offers a high density of memory resources relative to its compute allocation, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency single-thread execution. Given the 64.0 GB RAM capacity and average database operation performance of 2822.19 on Passmark, this instance is suited for relational databases, in-memory caching, mid-sized web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring substantial memory overhead.
